title: 9 new packings below record for n = 88–302 (s(n) bounds 1.4e-3 to 1.2e-2 below the reported side) + updated summary on all 26-10-07 upper bound changes: registration request
body:
**Update (2026-10-07, 17:00): 9 new or smaller packings.**

Five counts are new: 88, 199, 207, 236, 302. Four counts have smaller packings than those linked earlier in this thread, which they replace: 108 (was 10.920658939403, in the first folder), 179 (was 13.891312565741, in the first update), 180 (was 13.923635004252, in the first folder), 263 (was 16.740446480043, in the first update). For 108 and 180 the register now holds our earlier packing; these are smaller still.

For these 9 counts, `s(n) ≤ S_n`, where `S_n` is the exact rational side of our certificate:

| n | S_n (to 15 digits) | register now | difference |
|---|---|---|---|
| 88 | 9.882451030482136 | 9.888153053759 | 5.702e-03 |
| 108 | 10.909940073444877 | 10.920658939403 (ours) | 1.072e-02 |
| 179 | 13.883795490512187 | 13.895341069976 | 1.155e-02 |
| 180 | 13.917653417451476 | 13.923635004252 (ours) | 5.982e-03 |
| 199 | 14.617572173598040 | 14.618988956899 | 1.417e-03 |
| 207 | 14.887992258307747 | 14.893954634237 | 5.962e-03 |
| 236 | 15.867800839425540 | 15.872219025607 | 4.418e-03 |
| 263 | 16.740419679538775 | 16.742270262025 | 1.851e-03 |
| 302 | 17.881306218095808 | 17.885993892530 | 4.688e-03 |

**Certificates.** https://github.com/itsnaka/squish-certs/tree/e63e4e52b1728b6671b2f263c5e02a4aa79a39d3/squish-submission-2026-10-07b (commit e63e4e52b1728b6671b2f263c5e02a4aa79a39d3), one folder per n, in the same format as before: `nNNN.cert.json` (exact rational certificate, `s_exact` the exact side), `nNNN.cert.txt` (40 digits, Ellsworth's format), `nNNN.cert50.txt`, `nNNN.svg`, `check_packing_output.txt`. The repository's README lists our current packing for every count. The earlier folders, at their commits, are unchanged.

**Checking.** As before: SQUISH's exact checker (separating-axis theorem in exact rational arithmetic on every pair close enough to touch, and every square against the box) and David Ellsworth's `check_packing.py` (`Epsilon: 1E-40, Container: OK, Overlaps: NONE, VALID`) pass for all 9. A further squeeze of each (about 120 random perturbations at 1e-5 to 1e-3 of the side, each re-polished) lowered no side by more than 1e-11, except n = 263, whose certificate here already includes that squeeze (4e-10).

**Lineage.** Each step starts from the packing the previous one made. "(Kingbird's 41) -> 88, grafted" means the catalogue's s(41), improved in January 2026 after the s(88) record was built from it, grafted into that record; "(our 110) - 2" means our certified s(110) with two squares removed, "(Couzo's 180) - 1" Francisco Couzo's s(180) with one removed; "nearby search" is a search for a nearby smaller arrangement from the packing before it.

- n = 88: (Kingbird's 41) -> 88, grafted
- n = 108: (our 110) - 2 → nearby search
- n = 179: (Couzo's 180) - 1 → nearby search
- n = 180: (our 182) - 2 → nearby search
- n = 199: (Kingbird's 37) -> 199, grafted
- n = 207: (our 88) -> 207, grafted
- n = 236: (our 88) -> 236, grafted
- n = 263: (Couzo's 297) -> 263, carved → nearby search → squeeze
- n = 302: (our 88) -> 302, grafted

Seeds: the Kingbird catalogue's s(41) and s(37) for 88 and 199; Francisco Couzo's published s(180) and s(297) for 179 and 263; our own certified packings for 108 (from our 110) and 180 (from our 182); and our new 88 for 207, 236 and 302.

Credit: Nate Chaoweeraprasit, using SQUISH (SQuare-packing Using Iterative Shrink-Hopping).

**AI assistance.** SQUISH: solver, verification, and this filed issue was written with claude opus 5.5 for coding and research intentions; project directed, managed, reviewed, and steered by me


------
